thread:
anika: Heads-up — we discovered ~30 doc links still pointing to the old /v1 endpoints in the API reference and migration guide. Need to triage and prioritize which ones get redirects vs. straight edits.

samir: ugh. can you dump a list? I can take the SDK snippets and examples.

anika: pasted initial grep in the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/614 (WIP). main categories: quickstart snippets, embed migration examples, and three customer-facing guides.

mike: tagging docs-bot to run link-checker for the whole site? :mag:

docs-bot: link-checker report ready — 28 failures found in /api/, /guides/migration/, /examples/quickstart/. Full report: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/link-check-1729999999.html

elaine: prioritize customer-facing pages first (guides). If it's a stable redirect we should add a server-side 301 mapping, otherwise update the content.

jordan: for SDK snippets: prefer editing inline and adding a short note: "old v1 endpoint removed — use v2 client". Avoid redirects for code samples to prevent stale examples.

samir: agreed. I can open PRs for examples. Plan: 1) apply direct edits to snippets 2) add redirect mappings for marketing/guides 3) audit remaining API reference pages for backward-compatible aliasing.

anika: timeline? we promised a deprecation notice next week.

mike: can we get a hotfix release to add the redirect map entries? ops can deploy a config change in <30m once PR approved.

elaine: ops will need a canonical list in CSV: old_path,new_path,reason,owner. I'll own compiling that. Please drop items there.

samir: adding entries — examples PRs: #616 (python quickstart), #617 (node streaming), #618 (embeddings examples).

jordan: smoke tests — put a small test in docs-ci that loads the snippet page and runs the code block via our smoke runner. If code hits old endpoint the test should fail. I'll add a check in #620.

anika: good. For customer guides that reference model aliases (e.g., "redwood/old-chat-1"), we need to note the alias migration to the new canonical ids and mention fallback behavior. Which docs mention aliases? docs-bot, can you grep for "redwood/old"?

docs-bot: grep completed — occurrences found: /guides/migration/aliases.md (5), /api/model-catalog.md (3), /examples/legacy-models/README.md (2).

mike: I'll take /api/model-catalog.md and add an explicit alias table with recommended replacements + compatibility notes. PR #621.

elaine: checklist for each PR: (a) confirm code snippet compiles/runs, (b) update crosslinks, (c) add redirect if page is referenced externally, (d) if alias removed, add note with timeline. Put checklist as comment in PR template.

anika: can everyone drop one-liner on ownership in this thread so I can assemble the CSV?

samir: examples: #616,#617,#618 — owner: samir.

mike: api ref: #621 — owner: mike.

jordan: smoke tests and CI check: #620 — owner: jordan.

elaine: compiling CSV now. will ping when ready for ops.

anika: once ops deploys redirect config, we still need a post-deploy smoke: 1) try a couple old URLs, 2) ensure 301 to /v2 or note. jordan can add to post-deploy job.

jordan: yep, will add 3 checks: /api/old-endpoint -> 301, code snippet runs, model alias resolves to new id.

mike: small note: avoid mass-changing embedded code blocks where the behavior differs between v1/v2 (streaming framing). Add a compatibility note instead.

anika: good catch. we'll selectively edit.

docs-bot: deploy note — ops config PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/982 — please add mapping entries in infra/redirects/1729999999.csv before EOD.

elaine: CSV uploaded: infra/redirects/1729999999.csv. entries: 17 lines — I included reason & owner.

samir: PRs opened and linked in the main tracking issue #4321.

anika: thanks all. final: we should publish a short deprecation FAQ snippet in /guides/migration/faq.md summarizing redirects, expected breakage, and rollback instructions. I'll create a PR #622 and tag QA.

mike: :thumbsup: great.

docs-bot: thread archived to issue tracker #4321-migration-redirects (auto).
